correctness.rationale: The eleven complete ambiguity branches, positive multiplicities and total N^2 are derived by exact Walsh orthogonality on the coset pair {0,d}. The known Weyl diagonalization gives exact singular values. The lower bound uses r=min(|u+s|,|u-s|,|v+t|,|v-t|), H>=N-2+3r^2/2 for r<=2 and H>=N-2r+2r^2 for r>=2, with m<=2r; algebra and AM-GM yield sqrt(2N)-1. All eight equality cases are forced and directly checked against ALL branches. The script CHECK.py executed: 30 complete exact Gaussian-integer enumerations, five direct exact modular ranks for N=8, and 32 numerical evaluations of all eight sharp parameter locations. Independent finite checks do not stand in for the universal algebraic proof. The scope n>=3 makes every four-sign branch present.

value.rationale: This is an exact solution to the natural structured design problem of whether a second complex coordinate defect improves worst-direction Gabor linear tomography stability. It proves a sharp global NO-IMPROVEMENT theorem, classifies all eight equality cases including four genuinely separated supports, and gives a complete all-parameter eleven-level spectrum/rank discriminant. Split real-only and imaginary-only defects are each individually incomplete but jointly achieve the optimum, a substantive design insight. The result is not merely an existence construction or tiny numeric gain and does not claim optimality over arbitrary fiducials.
